金貝鼓以徒手演奏，鼓面為未處理生皮，外殼以硬木雕刻；演奏者透過不同擊打方式發出多: The djembe is played with the bare hands on a head of untreated rawhide, on a shell carved from hardwood; the player draws many different sounds from it by varying the stroke. Beginners should first get used to the rope-tuned shell and head, then practise taking a clear solo inside a large percussion ensemble. Traditionally it is played by men, often together with the dundun.
金貝鼓在西非傳統合奏中常與敦敦鼓一同演奏，並與沙克雷鼓、karignan、kes: In traditional West African ensemble the djembe is often played alongside the dundun, in a line-up that also takes in the shekere, the karignan and the kese kese; traditionally men play the djembe and the dundun and women play the other instruments. After the middle of the twentieth century it entered the national ballets and international tours of Guinea, Mali and Senegal, and it has appeared on Western stages, on recordings, in concerts filmed for documentaries, and in performances by Paul Simon and Cirque du Soleil.
金貝鼓為膜鳴高腳鼓，以徒手擊打皮面發聲，繩索調音。它能產生多種聲音，音量大，可在: The djembe is a membranophone goblet drum, sounded by striking the head with the bare hands and tuned with ropes. It can produce many different sounds and is loud, so it can solo clearly inside a large percussion ensemble; the Maninka describe a skilled player as able to 'make the drum speak', using it to tell of feelings rather than as a signalling drum. Compared with the dundun that usually accompanies it, and with beaded gourds, tube bells and basket rattles, the djembe is a solo instrument. The source gives no definite range, no means of controlling volume, and no account of how it differs from related instruments.
金貝鼓琴身以硬木雕刻，鼓面使用未經石灰處理的生皮，最常見為山羊皮。調音系統以繩索: The djembe's shell is carved from hardwood and its head is untreated rawhide, most often goatskin. The tuning system is made of rope and includes parts such as the rings; the source does not say what the rings are made of. Overall weight varies with the size and with the wood of the shell. Traditionally the drums are carved by hand in Mali, Guinea, Burkina Faso and Senegal with traditional woods and tools; later they were also machine-made elsewhere, using softer, less dense substitute woods such as mahogany, which the source says are less suitable than the traditional woods.
金貝鼓起源與曼丁哥鐵匠階級 Numu 有關，其分布可能隨 Numu 在第一千年遷: The djembe's origin is bound up with the Mandinka blacksmith caste, the Numu, and its spread may have followed Numu migrations in the first millennium; the traditional area is linked with the Mali Empire from 1230, and since there is no written record it remains unclear whether the drum predates the empire. Before the 1950s it was used mainly among local peoples. In 1952 Fodéba Keïta founded Les Ballets Africains, which toured with the support of Guinea's president Sékou Touré and brought the djembe into Western view. After Touré's death in 1984 several players moved to Europe and America to teach, and the 1991 documentary Djembefola and the 2007 film The Visitor widened its international recognition.
金貝鼓（Djembe）是一種繩索調音、皮面高腳鼓，屬於薩巴爾（Sabar）家族，: The djembe is a rope-tuned goblet drum with a skin head, belonging to the sabar family, Hornbostel–Sachs number 211.261.1. Its shell is hollowed from hardwood and its head is usually untreated goatskin, played with the bare hands. Traditionally it is played by men and used with the dundun in West African percussion ensembles; the Mandinka hold that a skilled player can make the drum 'speak', but the Malinké do not use it as a signalling drum.
